column1: # Control registry for the fixture apps. THIS IS THE ANSWER KEY.
# It lives OUTSIDE fixtures/apps/, which is the only directory serve.sh exposes,
# so it is not fetchable from the browser the explorer drives. It was previously
# served at /controls.tsv -- an answer key reachable by the thing being measured.
# Do not read this file into a session that will run the explorer, and never put
# any of it into the served files: probe.sh greps the source from outside, and the
# served HTML/CSS/JS carries no comments at all (a test enforces that).
#   class      defect class, for the floor check and authority scoping
#   probe      literal string that must be PRESENT for the defect to exist ("-" = none)
#   antiprobe  literal string that must be ABSENT ("-" = none). This is what makes
#              "armed" mean "defect present AND fix absent": several probes would
#              otherwise survive the repair they are meant to detect -- adding an
#              aria-label does not remove the button markup.
#   signature  what a run that found it must report

column6: signature
The status filter's Apply button does nothing: choosing a status and applying never changes the table.
Saving a position clears the entered quantity and shows success, but the value is not applied anywhere on screen.
A match rate is given to one decimal place with no denominator or sample size, implying precision its own basis cannot support.
A monetary amount is rendered with no currency, no thousands separator and one decimal place.
Positions reviewed: 0 is indistinguishable from unavailable data; nothing marks a missing value as missing.
An all-numeric date on a decision surface is ambiguous between day-first and month-first order.
A raw UUID appears in the Status column where a human-readable status belongs.
A section heading is an internal identifier in screaming snake case rather than the user's words.
Enum tokens are shown as status values and as dropdown options.
A request fails on load and logs a console error while the screen looks entirely healthy.
The focus indicator is removed globally, so keyboard traversal is invisible.
Icon-only info and delete buttons have no accessible name, and their targets are a few pixels tall.
Hint text sits at roughly 1.9:1 contrast, far below the 4.5:1 floor.
The Instrument column takes 44% of the table while Custodian reference is clipped at 90px; widths are inverted relative to content length.
Section headings are the same size as the page title, so the hierarchy is flat.
A prose paragraph runs the full window width with no measure cap, well past a readable line length.
A version-like column sorts lexically, so v10 files before v9.
Three mutually exclusive options are hidden behind a dropdown where radios would show all of them.
Position detail opens in a modal that hides the row it refers to, and the modal has no URL.
A destructive purge is styled as a quiet underlined link and sits beside the primary export action, with no confirmation and no undo.
A success toast fires before anything is persisted, and disappears after 1.2s.
An indeterminate spinner runs with no progress, no expectation set, and no distinction between slow and stuck.
The queue page is reachable only by typing the URL; nothing links to it and it offers no route back.
No orientation anywhere: no breadcrumb, no active nav state, no in-page back affordance.
An empty state says only "No records", conflating first-run, no-results and failure.
Validation fires on every keystroke, the error text is generic and far from the fields, and a failed submit clears every value the user typed.
A disabled action gives no explanation of what would enable it.
Fields rely on placeholders instead of persistent labels, and a date is a free-text box with no format guidance.
